16.name: Conceptual
16.description: You appreciate learning in an environment where you are allowed to think big, and integrate different concepts by understanding how they fit into the larger picture. In specific situations, you may also find yourself focussing on the task at hand, looking at the finer details without thinking too much about linking the learning to the wider context.

16.name: Contemplative
16.description: You like to take time to consolidate your thoughts in order to maximize your learning. At times you may also find yourself anxious to get on to "doing" rather than "thinking".

16.name: Experiential
16.description: You enjoy learning through trial and error using a "hands - on" approach to new experiences. At the same time, you are also open to taking the time and doing some research, before plunging in to a new task.

16.name: Flexible
16.description: You like to jump right into the task and learn by 'taking is as it comes'. In other times, you may find yourself rely on your favoured learning methods.

16.name: Logical
16.description: You learn efficiently when you are able to process new information in a systematic, methodical manner. There may also be situations when you enjoy learning organically, jumping around from one aspect to another.

16.name: Receptive
16.description: You may enjoy learning by seeking feedback from others around you. At the same time, in situations where recognition or ongoing support is not available, you will tend to find other ways and means to enhance your learning experience.

16.name: Resourceful
16.description: You are indifferent towards learning by finding innovative solutions or having a fixed set of pre-defined resources to learn from. You are able to adapt your learning approach depending upon the situation.

16.name: Social
16.description: You tend to seek interactions with your peers and colleagues to flourish in your learning experiences. In certain situations, you may also prefer to work independently and have the freedom to organise your own work in order to learn most effectively.

16.name: Structured
16.description: You enjoy learning in an organised and supportive environment, with clear objectives and readily available resources. You may also find yourself in situations where you will tend to learn better when you are not constantly being directed in what, when, where and how to learn.

props.text: Assessment of General Intellectual and Learning Efficacy (A.G..I.L.E.)

A.G.I.L.E
Your Guide To Enhancing Your Learning Efficacy
All Rights Reserved © The Talent Enterprise

Learning Agility is a competency or willingness to learn from experience and apply that learning to perform successfully in your area of work. An essential leadership attribute is the ability to remain open to new ways of thinking and to continuously learn new skills.

Learning-agile individuals tend to be more social, creative, focused, and resilient. They are less interested in accommodating others and are not afraid to challenge norms. Learning-agile behaviorsmatter to others; managers seem to value those who are less defensive and who are open to feedback; peers and direct reports appear to value those who are more reflective and willing to change.

An individual’s current skill-set seems to be of secondary importance when compared with their ability to learn new knowledge, skills, and behaviorsthat will equip them to respond to future challenges. There is thus a need to find, develop and retain talent that is continually able to give up skills, perspectives, and ideas that are no longer relevant, and learn new ones that are.

Additionally, every individual has their own unique approach to learning based on strengths, weaknesses, and preferences. It's commonly believed that most people favor some particular method of interacting with, taking in, and processing stimuli or information. 

This report enables you to identify your most and least preferred learning styles in order to thrive in your learning process.
DIMENSIONS OF LEARNING EFFICACY – AN OVERVIEW

Learning efficacy scores on each dimension have been computed keeping in view the enablers and derailers. All scores are normed with the relevant norm group for you.

Derailers are the behaviors that pull you back from performing to your best on that particular dimension, whereas enablers promote or encourage adequate or outstanding performance.
DIMENSIONS OF LEARNING EFFICACY

A growth mindset is one which includes the strong belief that people have the innate potential and capacity to develop for the better, if they so desire. It is a belief that change is possible, that if people invest the necessary effort, apply their energy and focus, they can improve their abilities and capabilities. This is in contrast to having a ‘rigid’ view of the world assuming that capabilities are relatively fixed, and hard to change, no matter what people do.

Strategic Orientation is the ability to link the long-range vision of self-determination to daily work, ranging from a simple understanding to a sophisticated awareness of the full impact of thinking and actions. Being able to identify patterns or connections and address key underlying issues.

Critical thinking is the ability to think clearly and rationally about what to do or what to believe. It includes the ability to engage in reflective and independent thinking. Someone with critical thinking skills is able to understand the logical connections between ideas. A critical thinker begins with the right approach, looks deeper and farther, asks complex questions, answers questions through different ways and reflects on them.
DIMENSIONS OF LEARNING EFFICACY

Creativity is the desire and orientation to innovate, generate new ideas and concepts, demonstrate original thinking and implement them at the workplace. Someone high in creativity often are motivated to identity new, different and / or unique ways of working. Creative people tend to be independent, nonconformist, unconventional, cognitively flexible and are likely to have wide interests. Someone high in creativity is likely to endorse the statement “It is important for me to be able to use my imagination at work”, and “I enjoy thinking of new ways to complete my work”.

Desire to develop entails having a passionate interest in gaining knowledge in one’s area of work, working hard to learn and improve skills, being curious and pursuing subjects of interest, applying learning strengths and finding ways to address learning challenges.

Curiosity is a strong orientation and interest in discovering more about work and the extent to which new learning is actively sought out in one’s role or broader work environment. It is characterised by thriving in situations where there is an opportunity to be inquisitive and investigating further. Curious people tend to endorse statements like “I normally ask the most questions at work” and reject ones such as “I don't concern myself with things not directly related to my job.”

Welcome to the A.G.I.L.E. Assessment. 

This questionnaire has a number of questions about your individual learning strengths and preferences. There are also 4 scenario – based questions, where you have to rank your preferred approach. In total, it is expected to take a maximum of 10 minutes for you to complete all of the questions.


Some things to remember: 
a) Do answer the survey as honestly as you can. Please remember that there are no ideal answers
b) Whilst completing the questions, respond instinctively with the first response that comes to your mind
c) Try and complete the questionnaire in one - go, preferably without any interruptions

Instructions:
Please read and consider each question individually, and answer it as directly as possible by clicking the button next to the choice you want. When you have answered every question on the page, click the "Next" button on the lower right of the screen to move on to the next page.

NOTE: You must answer every question on each page before you can move on.

If you have any questions or require any clarifications regarding this questionnaire, please write to us at surveys@thetalententerprise.com
